item.title: The Violet Protocol
item.content:encoded: Miss Bartlett arrives at Windy Corner and immediately revives Lucy’s anxiety over her past encounter with George Emerson in Florence. Lucy insists George means no harm, yet finds herself emotionally affected whenever he is near. Cecil’s rigid worldview clashes with the warmth of the Honeychurch family, while hidden memories, guilt, and unresolved attraction begin quietly reshaping Lucy’s emotions.

item.title: Algorithm of Class
item.content:encoded: Lucy’s engagement to Cecil begins unraveling as class tension, buried emotions, and George Emerson’s return disrupt the calm order of Windy Corner. A chaotic encounter at the Sacred Lake exposes the contrast between Cecil’s rigid sophistication and George’s untamed vitality. Haunted by secrets and social expectations, Lucy feels trapped between respectable society and a deeper, freer version of herself.

item.content:encoded: Now remember how PCA collapses data with 100 dimensions into a single dimension, wouldn't it be cool if this dimension was interpretable. AI is a powerful text predictor that generates answers by guessing the most likely next token based on patterns learned from massive amounts of human writing. - Context & attention: Your prompt and conversation become part of the model’s context, the information it can currently see. item.title: Most Node.js Apps Using ClamAV Have the Same Bug. Here's What It Is.
item.content:encoded:
Calling ClamAV from Node.js looks easy: spawn clamscan, check the exit code, done. But the standard implementation has a silent bug — exit code 2 means "scan could not complete," not "clean," and almost every custom wrapper collapses it into one of the other two outcomes. The result is a false-clean verdict on encrypted archives, permission-denied files, and timeouts. The fix is to model ClamAV's three real outcomes — Clean, Malicious, ScanError — as three explicit return values, and force the caller to handle ScanError as a security decision rather than a programming error. This article explains why this matters, what the failure looks like in production, and what a correct minimal wrapper looks like in practice.
